question: What were Great Britain's total balancing or constraint costs (in GBP) on 26 October 2026, a stormy day, according to NESO data or news coverage?
value: Summing NESO’s six GBP cost categories: £38,650,310.28 total balancing costs; the “Constraints” category alone was £36,530,868.70.
caveat: The constraints figure is included in the total balancing costs; do not add it to the total. News coverage’s figure of more than £561 million refers to October as a whole, not 26 October alone.

question: How many TWh of wind generation were curtailed (paid to switch off) in Great Britain in 2025, and what was the cost of these payments in GBP?
value: 10.241336 TWh (10,241,336 MWh); £382,108,508 in payments to constrain wind-farm output.
caveat: This is the sum of REF’s monthly Balancing Mechanism wind-farm constraint entries. Montel separately reports £363m in total Great Britain curtailment payments across renewables, so the totals differ by source/measure and the Montel figure is not a wind-only annual amount.

sources.quote: Over 10TWh of renewable electricity was curtailed in GB, enough to meet the demand of every domestic household in London in 2025. The total cost of curtailment payments was £363m, representing a 10% decrease year-on-year. The total cost of upward actions to replace lost wind power where necessary was at least £1bn, a 20% rise year-on-year. Over 98% of the curtailed volume and 94% of curtailment costs were due to turning down wind turbines in Scotland.
